title: Company-Elected Cash Offers on Uninstallable Replacements — Homeowner Service Contracts
content:
**Policy.** Under Bridgewell Homeowner Service Contracts, Bridgewell elects cash in place of a replacement it has authorized when no network contractor can install the like unit: every network contractor of the request's trade whose service ZIP codes include the ZIP code of the covered property is suspended. The offer is recorded on the request with the settlement basis "company elected", the re-quoted like-unit cost as its replacement cost, the company-elected cash amount as its amount, and an offer expiration date the tier's offer validity (calendar days) after the offer date.

**Issuing condition.** A company-elected cash-in-lieu offer is issued only once the most recent completion report on the contract, when it closes a Bridgewell replacement on a tier that pays a haul-away allowance, has that replacement's haul-away allowance on the records. Stated as a record test: where the most recent completion report on the contract closes a Bridgewell replacement on a tier whose haul-away allowance is above 0.00, the offer is not issued while that replacement's haul-away allowance is absent from the records.

**What the offer covers.** The offer states the cash that takes the place of the standing replacement; the credits owed on the request for Bridgewell's own service failures are not part of it.

## Recording the offer

The tool is `issue_company_cash_offer_eabc2067`. It is an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks it and then calls it. One call adds one company-elected cash offer to the service request's claim-handling history; recording the offer pays nothing and uses no benefit.

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `homeplan_contract_id` | the homeowner service contract number the request is placed under, as returned by the homeowner contract lookup | identifier |
| `homeplan_service_request_id` | the service request number of the replacement that cannot be installed, as returned by the claim-history lookup | identifier |
| `covered_item` | the item the offer concerns | one value from the list below |
| `replacement_cost` | the like-unit cost to record on the offer as its replacement cost | USD, rounded to 2 decimal places, positive |
| `amount` | the cash offered | USD, rounded to 2 decimal places, positive |
| `offer_expiration_date` | the last calendar day on which the offer may be accepted | date, YYYY-MM-DD |

Values accepted for `covered_item`: `heating_system` (the furnace, boiler or heat pump heating side), `cooling_system` (the central air conditioning), `ductwork` (heating and cooling ducts), `plumbing_leak` (an interior water supply or drain leak), `plumbing_stoppage` (an interior drain stoppage), `water_heater` (the water heater), `electrical` (the interior electrical system), `ceiling_fan` (a ceiling fan), `garbage_disposal` (the garbage disposal), `whirlpool_tub` (the whirlpool bathtub motor and pump), `refrigerator` (the kitchen refrigerator), `oven_range_cooktop` (the oven, range or cooktop), `dishwasher` (the dishwasher), `built_in_microwave` (the built-in microwave), `clothes_washer` (the clothes washer), `clothes_dryer` (the clothes dryer), `garage_door_opener` (the garage door opener).

**Return.** On success the tool returns `offer_reference` (the offer record reference), `homeplan_service_request_id` (the request it was made on), `settlement_basis` (always `company_elected`), `amount` (USD, 2 decimal places), `offer_expiration_date` (YYYY-MM-DD) and `status`, which reads "offered" when recorded. The request then shows the open offer, its amount and the last day it may be accepted.

*Illustration (hypothetical):* with a 30-day offer validity, an offer recorded on 2026-03-01 carries `offer_expiration_date` 2026-03-31.
